Describe raw impact estimates

Source: R/inputs.R
cm_impacts.Rd

One impact table holds the estimates of one outcome, one row per estimate. A disease can have several rows (e.g. from several studies, or crude and adjusted), and a row can be about a combination of diseases or a subgroup. There are two kinds of impact table:

Usage

cm_impacts(
  disease,
  value,
  ...,
  among = NA_character_,
  adjusted_for = NA_character_,
  measure = NULL,
  study = NA_character_,
  source = NA_character_,
  note = NA_character_,
  label = NULL,
  units = NULL
)

Arguments

disease

Character vector of disease ids or combinations ("a;b").

value

Numeric raw impacts.

...

Not used (arguments of earlier versions give a message). The arguments after it must be named.

among, adjusted_for

Optional subgroups and adjustment sets (see What a row means).

measure

NULL (default) for additive impacts; for event impacts, one measure per row or recycled.

study, source, note

Optional study label, citation and note.

label, units

Optional table-level metadata (e.g. label = "milk yield loss", units = "% of yield"), carried into the results.

Value

A cm_impacts data frame (attributes label, units and kind, "additive" or "event").

Details

  • Additive impacts (no measure): amounts in the outcome's own units, the same for every row (e.g. kg of milk, percent of yield, days, a welfare score). The package does not convert units; results come back in the units supplied. Adjust them with deconflate().

  • Event impacts (measure given): comparisons of the risk of an event (e.g. death or culling), as hazard ratios ("HR"), rate ratios ("rate_ratio"), risk ratios ("RR"), odds ratios ("OR") or risk differences ("RD"), which can be mixed. Adjust them with deconflate(..., event_model = TRUE) (snapshot hazard model).

What a row means

The model has an impact for each disease and an interaction for each combination that appears in disease. A row compares animals with all the diseases in disease against animals with none of them (for one disease: with against without), within the subgroup among (as in cm_associations(), including "no others", e.g. "only this disease against healthy animals").

  • Crude (empty adjusted_for): the difference in the outcome between the two groups (event impacts: the ratio or difference of their hazards or risks).

  • Adjusted (adjusted_for names diseases, separated by ";"): additive impacts are coefficients of a linear regression of the outcome on the disease (for a combination: its members, their smaller combinations and the combination itself) and the diseases in adjusted_for; event impacts are comparisons within strata of those diseases (for a combination, the interaction contrast), combined with Mantel-Haenszel-type weights. "all" means every other disease and combination term of the model: the row is then the term's own value (a combination adjusted for all is its interaction; for event impacts this holds for hazard and rate ratios). Within a subgroup among naming present diseases, it is the sum of the term and the terms that combine it with those diseases (e.g. a among c, adjusted for all, is the impact of a plus the a;c interaction, when the model has one). Names that are not diseases of the model are factors outside the model, ignored with a note.

Every disease needs at least one row of its own (for no effect: 0 for additive impacts and risk differences, 1 for ratios). The rows must determine every impact and interaction; deconflate() says which are not determined otherwise. Several rows about the same impacts are fitted together by weighted least squares (see deconflate()).

A Cox hazard ratio estimated over follow-up is not exactly a snapshot comparison (see deconflate(), "Event impacts"); entering one is an approximation and the user's assumption. Risk ratios, odds ratios and risk differences refer to the period of the overall risk given to deconflate().

Examples

cm_impacts(c("d1", "d2", "d3"), c(2.5, 5, 7.5), label = "yield", units = "%")
#>   row disease among adjusted_for measure value study source note
#> 1   1      d1  <NA>         <NA>    <NA>   2.5  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#> 2   2      d2  <NA>         <NA>    <NA>   5.0  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#> 3   3      d3  <NA>         <NA>    <NA>   7.5  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
# Two estimates for d1, and the interaction of d1 and d2
cm_impacts(c("d1", "d1", "d2", "d3", "d1;d2"), c(2.5, 2.1, 5, 7.5, 1),
           adjusted_for = c(NA, "d2", NA, NA, "all"), units = "%")
#>   row disease among adjusted_for measure value study source note
#> 1   1      d1  <NA>         <NA>    <NA>   2.5  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#> 2   2      d1  <NA>           d2    <NA>   2.1  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#> 3   3      d2  <NA>         <NA>    <NA>   5.0  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#> 4   4      d3  <NA>         <NA>    <NA>   7.5  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#> 5   5   d1;d2  <NA>          all    <NA>   1.0  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
# Event impacts: culling, with mixed measures
cm_impacts(c("d1", "d2", "d3"), c(1.5, 1.3, 0.04), measure = c("HR", "RR", "RD"),
           label = "culling")
#>   row disease among adjusted_for measure value study source note
#> 1   1      d1  <NA>         <NA>      HR  1.50  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#> 2   2      d2  <NA>         <NA>      RR  1.30  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#> 3   3      d3  <NA>         <NA>      RD  0.04  <NA>   <NA> <NA>
